Constructivism in international relations is where people come up with ideas, introduce them and establish linkages with other people around the world. As more and more people accept this idea, it produces a cascading effect, which brings attention in the realm of international politics. Hence, when acceptance reaches some point, internalisation will occur, where people will be forced to make changes to the structure of the system to acknowledge this issue.
